title: Streaming ergonomics and SSO auth patterns triage for client libraries
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Summary: Triage and prioritize a consolidated set of enterprise customer requests about client library streaming ergonomics (reconnect/backpressure/partial-result API shapes) and SSO/auth patterns (SSO for service accounts, token scoping, rotation, audit-friendly auth flows).

Background: Over the last quarter we've received 18 customer signals (CUs: FinCorp, HealthAI, Adlytics, and three stealth customers) asking for improved streaming parity across SDKs (Python, Go, Java, TypeScript), explicit reconnect semantics for long-lived streams, and clearer enterprise auth primitives (SAML-backed SSO for service accounts, short-lived scoped tokens, and explicit audit log hooks). Many customers cite production incidents caused by unclear retry semantics and lack of token rotation primitives in our client libs.

Goals: 1) Define a prioritized set of fixes/features for 2026.04 client-libs release that materially reduce integration friction for enterprise customers. 2) Produce ergonomics patterns and API proposals that engineering can implement without destabilizing the runtime. 3) Identify security review and infra dependencies early to avoid release slippage.

Scope (in-scope): streaming API surface shape changes, client reconnection/backpressure recommendations, per-language idiomatic examples, auth patterns for SSO/service accounts/token rotation, opt-in audit hooks.

Out of scope: full redesign of server-side streaming protocol, breaking changes to existing public stable endpoints without migration path.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal doc with wireframes and API signatures for streaming reconnect/backpressure approved by ENG and Design
Compatibility matrix showing per-language impact and migration notes for breaking changes
Implementation plan with estimated eng work and clear infra dependencies (ENG owners assigned)
Security review completed for SSO/service-account patterns and token rotation design
Customer validation sessions scheduled with top three customers and follow-up triage recorded
decision_log: 2026-01-15: Decided to prefer non-breaking additive APIs where possible; only add optional params for reconnect behavior rather than swapping call signatures (decision by Maya S., Liam O., Priya N.)

2026-01-22: Agreed on three auth patterns to support: (1) scoped short-lived tokens via KMS-backed rotation, (2) SSO-to-service-account mapping (SAML/OIDC bridge), (3) retained API keys for legacy customers with clear deprecation path (engineering prefers #1 + #2)
2026-01-29: Prioritization rubric chosen: Customer impact (40%), Implementation effort (30%), Security/compliance risk (20%), Strategic resonance (10%).
